source.title: Automatically Identifying Local and Global Circuits with Linear Computation Graphs
source.authors: Xuyang Ge; Fukang Zhu; Wentao Shu; Junxuan Wang; Zheng-Fu He; Xi-Peng Qiu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE and Transcoder feature-attribution analysis to examine an induction circuit and its relationship to a previous-token head in GPT-2 Small. This is a different method from the original work.
record.gate_note: The study examines induction behavior in selected examples, but does not report training-time measurements, a loss-curve bump, or a measure of in-context learning loss by token position. Its general statements about induction heads accounting for most in-context learning are attributed to prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: In GPT-2 Small, a model with MLPs rather than an attention-only toy model, the study traces one curated induction example with SAE/Transcoder attribution. Its own results bear on V1's mechanism: a previous-token head (L2A.H2) builds 'Web'-Preceding features, which key the QK attention of induction head L5A.H1, which then copies 'M'. This is a new setting and a different method. The study is mainly a methods paper, and the induction analysis is one demonstration.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main conclusion concerns the method: SAEs plus Transcoders give a linear computation graph, and Hierarchical Attribution yields finer-grained circuits. The induction result is a demonstration that 'Web' and 'Web'-Preceding features (the latter built by a previous-token head) drive an induction head's attention. They note their analysis is input-specific and may not generalize.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE and Transcoder feature attribution and circuit tracing on selected GPT-2 Small inputs; it does not reproduce the original training-dynamics measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The analysis is specific to selected inputs; the authors state that it may not generalize to other settings.
record.problems: The induction analysis uses selected examples and largely qualitative feature attribution; it does not report uncertainty estimates or a causal intervention on the identified heads. The authors state that the analysis is input-specific and may not generalize.

untested.parts: Attention-only small transformers; generality beyond one curated WebM input and two IOI prompts; causal ablation of the head composition (attribution only).
No measure of in-context learning or of induction heads' share of it.
No variation of data or training.

missing.what: In IOI circuits, the SAE induction features map onto induction heads L5A.H5 and L6A.H9. Preceding features map onto previous-token heads L2A.H2, L3A.H2 and L4A.H1. This is further evidence of induction/previous-token composition in GPT-2 Small.

record.verdict_notes: The record's second V1 label (limits_scope) has been dropped. Input-specificity and the absence of attention-only models are untested parts, not results showing the version fails. The study repeats the claim that induction heads drive most in-context learning only as a citation of Olsson et al., so that does not count as a test of V3. The study's own number for the bracket circuit is irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The analysis is on GPT-2 Small, not a small attention-only transformer. It does not ablate or otherwise causally test the proposed head composition, and examines selected inputs rather than a broad set of sequences.
No training-time emergence, abruptness, in-context learning gain, or training-loss bump is measured.
The study does not measure how much in-context learning in large transformers is explained by induction heads.
The induction analysis is on GPT-2 Small; it does not test prevalence across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
The study does not vary training data or setup to test effects on induction-head formation or in-context learning.
It does not compare few-shot task learning with token-copying behavior or assess which mechanisms carry few-shot learning.
The study does not measure training transitions or test whether induction-head formation consists of separate or overlapping phases.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Interpreted an induction feature in the IOI circuit
rows.measure: Token logit enhanced by the induction feature
rows.value: The feature enhances the logit of and, although the actual next token is not and
rows.note: The authors describe this as an induction feature; the result is an example of its predicted continuation not matching the actual continuation.
rows.check: The induction feature at the second 'John' predicts 'and', the token after the first 'John'. This is correct [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour, even though it is not the actual next token. State 'observed' is right; the record's note could mislead readers into reading it as a failure.

source_check.correct: At the second John in sJohn, an induction feature increases the logit of and, the continuation after the first John. Observed in GPT-2 Small; remove the attention-only V1 link.
source_check.problem: The copying interpretation is correct, but it does not establish V1 in attention-only transformers.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 Small, single curated WebM input and IOI prompts, SAE/Transcoder attribution
relationships.reason: Previous-token head L2A.H2 forms 'Web'-Preceding features (r5). These drive QK attention of induction head L5A.H1 (r4), which copies 'M' (35.0% + 33.0% OV share; r1–r3, r6). An induction feature also predicts the [B] token in IOI (r7).
relationships.display_finding: L2A.H2 produced preceding-token features that drove L5A.H1 to copy 'M', with OV shares of 35.0% and 33.0%; an induction feature also predicted the continuation token in IOI prompts.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: GPT-2 Small, single curated WebM input and IOI prompts, SAE/Transcoder attribution
labels.reason: Rows r1–r7 report induction behavior in GPT-2 Small with MLPs. V1 explicitly concerns small attention-only transformers, so these rows do not meet the same-kind-of-system requirement. They support an extension of the mechanism, not a verdict on V1 as written.

relation.reason: Its own attribution results examine induction behavior and its upstream mechanism; it reports substantive circuit findings beyond method performance.

tranche.reason: The study reports feature-level induction and previous-token composition in GPT-2 Small with MLPs, a setting outside V1's attention-only architecture.

source_check.notes: The synthesis statement correctly acknowledges the architecture mismatch. The percentages describe attribution shares on one curated input; the authors explicitly caution that input-specific circuits may not generalize.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small, selected WebM and IOI examples
reader_labels.reason: The reported feature contributions, Web-to-Web-Preceding attention pattern, and previous-token-head path support an induction-like composition in these examples (r1–r7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The induction analysis is input-specific and does not establish that the same circuit generalizes across sequences or in attention-only models (r1–r7).
